brief:
Tonight is Legs A, and every number on your cards is the same one you saw yesterday. You have not trained since Friday's Pull A, so there is no new evidence, and a number that changes without new evidence is just noise. Leg press opens at 200 and tops at 240. Everything else holds its weight and asks for one more rep than you got on 20 August.

One correction I owe you, because it was on your card in my handwriting. Yesterday's leg curl note said you hit fifteen at 142.5 on 20 August. You did not. You hit fifteen at 127.5, then thirteen and thirteen at 142.5. The numbers tonight do not change — finishing the opener at the top of its range is what earns 142.5 across the slot — but the sentence explaining them was wrong and now it is right.

The fourth leg curl set. My recovery trainer wanted three tonight and asked me to name in writing who owns the fourth, because you have twice written that a set count was too high. Here is the name: you do. On 23 August you were shown a card setting Legs A to four leg curl sets and Legs B to three, and you tapped yes. That is your decision, not mine, and it stands until you change it. If you want it back to three, say so and I will put a card up.

One new card: your incline curl on Pull B has run ten, ten, nine on four straight Pull B nights since July. The first two sets top out every time and only the third one falls short, so it goes to two sets — the same fix you accepted for the rope pushdown. The four cards from yesterday are still waiting for a tap.

Still open, still not something I can put on a card: there is no anti-rotation core movement anywhere in the app's 37-exercise list, so the corrective work you asked about on 17 August cannot be prescribed until that list itself changes. And I still do not know whether Push A on 27 August ran short because of the clock or your legs. Tell me and I will use it.

flags.note: Correction: yesterday's leg curl card said you hit fifteen at 142.5 on 20 August. You hit fifteen at 127.5, then thirteen twice at 142.5. Tonight's numbers are unchanged; the explanation on the card is now accurate.
The fourth leg curl set tonight is yours: you accepted a card on 23 August setting Legs A to four sets and Legs B to three. Say the word and I will put up a card to take it back to three.

Your leg extension is not changing tonight and there is no card for it: it looks like the leg curl and cable crunch rep-range cards on your phone, but it has climbed from 142.5 for fourteen in July to 150 for thirteen on 20 August, so it is still moving on its own and keeps its twelve-to-fifteen range.
Nothing has been logged since Pull A on 28 August, so every weight and rep tonight is identical to yesterday's review — no new session, no new numbers.
This is your first leg session since 20 August, eleven days ago, and you have had two full rest days back to back.

Still open, and still not something I can put on a card: there is no anti-rotation core movement anywhere in the app's 37-exercise list, so the corrective work you asked about on 17 August cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.

Push A on 27 August ran 37 minutes and ended after one set of overhead triceps, against 56 minutes for the same session on 17 August — no number has been changed because of it, and I still would like to know whether that was the clock or your legs.
Meso 2, week 2 of 4, a build block — this is the part of the cycle where work goes on, not off.

proposals.why: Your last four Pull B nights ran the incline curl at exactly ten, ten, nine — the same three numbers on 21 and 28 July and again on 15 and 25 August — so the first two sets hit the top of the range every single time and only the third falls short, which is the one thing stopping this slot from ever moving; this makes it two sets, the same fix you accepted on the rope pushdown.

Your leg curl asks twelve to fifteen reps on Legs A but ten to twelve on Legs B, and it is the same machine at the same 142.5 on both — on 20 August your best Legs A set at that weight was thirteen, which is inside the range but not the top, so the weight can never move, while the identical 142.5 for twelve on Legs B on 16 August is the top of its range and earns the next step; this makes Legs A ten to twelve so the only hamstring work on that day can actually progress.

The cable crunch asks twelve to fifteen and you finished at thirteen on Legs A and twelve on Legs B, both at 60 lb, so the stack has nothing that can ever move it — and unlike the hanging leg raise, which carries no weight and needs the high range you accepted, this one is loaded, so ten to twelve makes the twelves you already do earn the next plate.

Same change on the other leg day, and they belong together — the Legs B cable crunch sits at the same 60 lb and finished at twelve on 16 August, so leaving it at twelve to fifteen would freeze it on one day while the other one climbs.

You asked on 28 August why Pull A calls for three face pull sets when you think two is right, and you did two that night — Pull B already runs two, so this makes the two days agree with each other and with you.

overrides.reason: You finished ten reps at 180 last time, which is the top of the range, and 200 is the smallest step this machine makes; the top set stays at 240 because that is the ceiling both trainers agreed on.
The weight stays at 17.5 because nine, nine and eight never reached the top of the range and the next dumbbell up is 20, which is too big a jump to have earned.

On 20 August you finished fifteen at 127.5, the top of the range, and then held thirteen twice at 142.5 — topping the opener is what moves the whole slot to 142.5 tonight instead of starting light again. The fourth set is the one you accepted on 23 August.
Both sets stopped at thirteen inside a twelve to fifteen range, so tonight asks for the reps before it asks for more weight.
Twelve and twelve is the floor of the range, so this steps by one rep at the same weight.
Thirteen and thirteen sits mid-range, so one more rep each; fifteens are what buy the next step up.
Three sets, not four, and one more rep on each at the same 300 — the next pin on this machine is 320 and that is too big a jump from thirteen, thirteen and twelve.
Three flat thirteens with no drop-off on the last set, so this asks fourteen; the small micro plate waits until you are finishing fifteens.
Bodyweight, so the ask is reps only: you got thirteen then twelve on 20 August, so tonight is thirteen and thirteen.

dissent.progression: Four sets at 142.5 — 14, 13, 13, 12 — held unchanged from the standing sheet because no new leg curl row exists.
dissent.recovery: Three sets at 142.5 — 14, 13, 13 — cutting the fourth set on the grounds that he logged only three sets on 20 August and has twice written that a prescribed set count was too high.
dissent.why: Recovery is right about the pattern and wrong about this lift, and I can see that only because I can read a file its slice does not carry. It asked me to name in writing who owns the fourth set. He does. On 23 August he was shown a card that set Legs A to four leg curl sets and Legs B to three, and he accepted it — that is in decisions.json with a timestamp. Cutting it now would be overriding his own tap in the name of listening to him, which is the opposite of listening. The two seats do not differ on load at all: both want 142.5 across the slot and the same rep figures on the sets they share, so this is purely about whether his own accepted decision survives the night. It does. Recovery's underlying point — that set counts he questions get re-imposed and nobody names an owner — is correct and worth more than a set, so I have put the ownership on the card itself and in the brief, and told him plainly that one word puts a card up to take it back to three. Its second finding, that the 20 August timestamps were entered from memory and cannot support a fatigue read, I accept outright: no number tonight rests on that session's timing.
